description: A team of students exploring space, science, and technology. We combine technical expertise and creativity to develop meaningful solutions for global challenges through the NASA Space Apps Challenge.
summary: AstroVitals is an offline-capable, interactive astronaut self-health assessment and decision-support tool designed to address the health challenges of human spaceflight. We developed a platform that enables astronauts to perform guided health check-ins, monitor vital signs, assess vision and reaction performance, and visualize their health status through an interactive 3D-inspired human body map. The system combines personal health baselines, historical trends, and a compound-hazard rules engine to identify potential health concerns and suggest appropriate countermeasures. It also provides crew health overviews, simulated wearable data, radiation monitoring, and structured medical reports. AstroVitals addresses the five major hazards of human spaceflight by making health information more accessible and actionable, even when communication with Earth is limited. This is important because early awareness and informed health decisions are essential for protecting astronaut well-being during long-duration missions, particularly future missions to Mars.
details: AstroVitals is an offline-capable astronaut self-health assessment tool designed to support crew health monitoring during space missions. It allows astronauts to perform guided health check-ins, monitor vital indicators, visualize health conditions through an interactive human body map, and track changes against personal baselines. Its compound-hazard rules engine analyzes health trends and provides countermeasure guidance based on mission conditions, including communication delays during Mars missions. By combining interactive visualization, health tracking, and crew readiness monitoring, AstroVitals aims to help astronauts identify potential health concerns earlier and make more informed decisions. The project focuses on accessibility, offline functionality, and practical decision support for long-duration human spaceflight.
